TGA_specimen_preparation: air-dried fabric cut into approximately 2 mm squares; platinum cell with platinum lid
TGA_preconditioning: Heat from room temperature to 100 C at 10 C/min; hold for 20 min; then the stated 10 or 20 C/min ramp to 600 C.

treatment_chemistry: Fyrol 76 vinyl phosphonate oligomer (FYR) and/or N-methylolacrylamide (NMA), ammonium persulfate initiated
treatment_method: Base fabric cleaned using 0.2% anionic surfactant, then ethanol/benzene (1:1) Soxhlet extraction and air drying. Pad with aqueous FYR/NMA bath and ammonium persulfate at 10% of monomer weight; approximately 80% pickup. Air dry, steam at 100 C for 10 min, air dry, wash in distilled water at 80 C for 30 min, vacuum dry and store over silica gel.
source_title: Pad-Steam Treatments of Cotton Fabrics with Vinyl Phosphonate Oligomers and/or N-Methylolacrylamide and Thermal Behavior of the Treated Fabrics
source_location: Original Japanese article pp 272-277; Tables 1-3 and experimental sections 2.1-2.5.
limitations: Original publisher PDF methods and Tables 1-3 visually reviewed. NMA-4 LOI conflicts (21.4 table versus 21.5 prose) and remains held. DTA endotherm/exotherm peaks are not DTG maxima. Authors To/Tf describe main weight-loss boundaries, not T5/T10; only unambiguous TG Tmax/R600 included. Grafting-efficiency formula is not recalculated. Initial thermal prehold is not aging or laundering. Two ramps count as one state.
journal: Journal of the Japan Research Association for Textile End-Uses

pairing_evidence: Exact untreated/FYR/NMA/F/N sample codes link preparation and LOI Table 1 to both TG Tables 2/3. Two TG ramps are repeat conditions of one prepared material state, not extra samples. Preparative hot-water extraction is not a durability-wash series.

limitations: Three states (LPU@COT, LPU/DCD@COT, SiO2-LPU/DCD@COT) are held for conflicting LOI prose versus Table 5. Values for these five retained states come from the original tables. Figure 5 mixed LPU/DCD impregnation is 30 min while prose says 15 min; neither is transferred to comparator dwell times.

treatment_method: Industrial aramid fabric from Tayho Advanced Materials was sequentially pretreated with toluene, acetone and deionized water in an HL-20 annular centrifugal extractor for a reported 3 h; whether this duration applies per liquid is not specified. The fabric was dried in a vacuum oven at 110 °C for 6 h. Fabric was then immersed in deionized water or the specified phosphoric acid solution at 40 °C for 24 h, repeatedly rinsed with deionized water to neutral and oven-dried at 80 °C for an unreported duration. E-51 epoxy and Z-6018 phenyl propyl polysiloxane were mixed at a 6:4 mass ratio using an unspecified amount of acetone, with a phosphazene catalyst of unspecified identity and loading, reacted at 15 °C for 5 h and rotary-evaporated for 2 h. The modified epoxy, 4-MHHPA and DMP-30 were mixed at 100:85.68:0.5 by mass and degassed at 70 °C and −0.08 MPa for 1 h. Twelve fabric layers were laid up by hand and cured in a JZ-5009 flat vulcanizing press at 5 MPa, 100 °C for 2 h and 150 °C for 5 h. Final fabric/resin mass or volume fractions, fabric areal density and weave are not reported.

composition: Table I nominal formulation: soy flour 100 (20 g basis, under the printed Starch header); glycerol 5; GA 50; jute 75; MMT 5. GA and MMT are stated relative to soy flour. treatment_chemistry: Soy flour/glycerol resin with nominal GA 50% and MMT 5% relative to soy flour, applied to washed/dewaxed/alkali-treated jute fabric
treatment_method: Jute fabric was washed in 2% soap solution at 70 °C for 1 h, rinsed with distilled water and vacuum-dried at 100 °C for 12 h. It was dewaxed in alcohol/benzene 1:2 for 72 h at 50 °C, washed and dried for 12 h, then treated with 5% w/v NaOH for 30 min at 30 °C, repeatedly rinsed, immersed in distilled water overnight, rinsed again and vacuum-dried at 70 °C for 12 h before desiccator storage. Soy flour and deionized water were mixed 1:10 by mass and glycerol was added. The slurry was mechanically stirred for 4 h at source-stated 55 °C with an unresolved indexed uncertainty suffix, cooled to source-stated 35 °C with the same suffix and mixed with the specified GA amount for 5 min. For MMT states, clay was dispersed in water, magnetically stirred for 6 h and sonicated for 30 min at source-stated 0.5 cycle and 140 l m wave amplitude (unit as indexed) before addition to the pre-cured resin. Surface-modified fabric was dipped for 24 h at 25 °C, placed on a Teflon-coated glass plate and dried on a heating plate at 60–70 °C. Impregnated fabric was stacked on 15 levels in a 3 mm metal mould and compression-moulded in a Santec press at 80 °C and 100 MPa; pressing duration is unreported. The final laminate thickness is reported as 3 mm.

treatment_method: Yantai Spandex meta-aramid was scoured with two water rinses at 60°C, then two ethanol and two acetone rinses at room temperature, and dried at room temperature for 24 h. For the coating solution, 10.5 g meta-aramid per 100 mL DMAc and 6 g CaCl2 were stirred at 130°C for 4 h until uniform; 4.5 g TPP per 100 mL was added. DOPO (1.8 g, reported as 0.008 mol) was stirred in 380.0 mL ethanol to obtain solution D. The three prepared mixtures were mixed and stirred together in unreported proportions and the resulting hybrid sol was aged for 2 h. A small, unquantified amount of penetrant JFC-1 was added; cut fabric was immersed in the corresponding bath at room temperature for 2 h and cured in a PHG-9036A oven at 100 °C for 5 min. No post-treatment rinse or durability wash is stated.

treatment_chemistry: hydroxylamine hydrochloride followed by monoethanolamine, then pre-oxidation in air
treatment_method: Commercial Jilin PAN fibers washed with alcohol. Treat in 40 g/L hydroxylamine hydrochloride at 80 C for 2 h; adjust pH to 5 with anhydrous sodium carbonate; wash and dry. Then reflux in 30 mg/L monoethanolamine at 90 C for 2 h with stirring; cool and wash with deionized water at 70 C. Apply unspecified tension and pre-oxidize in air from 170 C to 250 C at 1 C/min, hold 10 min. Source concentration 30 mg/L retained without correction.

treatment_method: Soak 100% cotton fabric in 20% NaOH solution for 10 min, wash with distilled water until neutral, and dry at 70 °C to obtain the source control cotton with reduced crystallinity. Synthesize AATMPEG by heating source-reported 0.1 mol (29.9 g, 50%) ATMP at 130 °C for 30 min to approximately 75% concentration; add 0.2 mol (12.4 g) ethylene glycol and react at 130 °C for 2 h, then add 0.2 mol (12 g) urea and react at 130 °C for 1.5 h. Purify with anhydrous ethanol and dry at 70 °C. Prepare 25 wt% aqueous AATMPEG with 5 wt% dicyandiamide; soak control cotton at bath ratio 1:20 in a 70 °C oscillator for 1 h. Dip and roll twice to 100% liquid pickup, cure at 185 °C for 5 min, wash with distilled water and dry at 70 °C to constant weight.

composition: 100% cotton fabric, 127.75 g/m², Chongqing Chaotianmen Market; control and treated states share the explicit NaOH pretreatment
treatment_chemistry: AATMPEG: P/N flame retardant containing phosphate ester and ammonium phosphate groups, synthesized from amino trimethylene phosphonic acid, ethylene glycol and urea; 5 wt% dicyandiamide catalyst
treatment_method: Soak 100% cotton fabric in 20% NaOH solution for 10 min, wash with distilled water until neutral, and dry at 70 °C to obtain the source control cotton with reduced crystallinity. Synthesize AATMPEG by heating source-reported 0.1 mol (29.9 g, 50%) ATMP at 130 °C for 30 min to approximately 75% concentration; add 0.2 mol (12.4 g) ethylene glycol and react at 130 °C for 2 h, then add 0.2 mol (12 g) urea and react at 130 °C for 1.5 h. Purify with anhydrous ethanol and dry at 70 °C. Prepare 25 wt% aqueous AATMPEG with 5 wt% dicyandiamide; soak control cotton at bath ratio 1:20 in a 70 °C oscillator for 1 h. Dip and roll twice to 100% liquid pickup, cure at 185 °C for 5 min, wash with distilled water and dry at 70 °C to constant weight.

composition: Twill-weave cotton fabric, 308 g/m², supplied by Jiangsu Shayin Group
sample_state: cot_Si, initial silica hydrosol and HDTMS treated cotton
treatment_chemistry: Methyltrimethoxysilane (MTMOS), tetraethoxysilane (TEOS), and hexadecyltrimethoxysilane (HDTMS), with CTAC/Tween 60 surfactants; cot_Si is the phosphorus-free silica hydrosol treatment
treatment_method: Disperse MTMOS in 100 mL distilled water with surfactants using a FA25 FLUKO disperser. Acid-hydrolyze for 4 h, then add TEOS dropwise and react for 2 h; modify the sol with HDTMS. Source optimization identifies 1.5 g MTMOS, 2.5 g TEOS, CTAC:Tween 60 = 2:3, surfactant dosage 0.9% (denominator unstated), pH 3 and 30 °C synthesis. cot_Si is explicitly pure silica hydrosol, without ammonium biphosphate; HDTMS amount and the exact cot_Si-specific quantities are not separately stated. Pad at 2 kg/cm² nip pressure, dry at 80 °C for 5 min and cure for 5 min; optimization captions specify 130 °C. Condition at 25 ± 2 °C and 65% humidity for 24 h. No durability washing reported.

Related journal Table 2 repeats LOI 17.4 and Table 1 repeats R600 11.4 for silica-only fabric, but its other state LOIs conflict with the proceedings or internally, so control and phosphorus-treated states remain held. Preparation includes water rinse, documented by W3 after-rinse mass; rinse parameters and post-rinse drying are not stated. Exact monomer synthesis stoichiometry/time/temperature are not reported in this paper.

composition: 100% natural cotton fabric, 120 g/m², Texmar Company, Egypt. Weave and yarn specifications are not stated.
treatment_chemistry: PVA and melamine salt of tannic phosphate; Table 1 reports 10% PVA plus 30% MTP
treatment_method: Wash cotton fabric with deionized water and dry at 60 °C for 1 h before use. Prepare MTP by stirring 50 g phosphoric acid with 20 g tannic acid at 100 °C for 1 h to form tannic phosphate. Disperse 30 g melamine in 500 mL methanol; add tannic phosphate solution dropwise over 30 min, maintain the hot plate at 120 °C and react for 6 h. Filter, wash with methanol, dry at room temperature for 72 h and grind to powder. The source states that the beaker containing deionized water and PVA was heated to 150 °C for 30 min using a hot plate with mechanical stirring at 650 rpm. Whether 150 °C is the actual solution temperature or the hotplate setting is unresolved. PVA molecular weight is 115000 g/mol and degree of polymerization 1700-1800. Add MTP to the PVA solution under continuous stirring at 70 °C; use the Table 1 C7 formulation of 10% PVA and 30% MTP. Soak fabric in the finishing solution at 70 °C for 10 min; pad three times to 90% pickup, dry at 100 °C for 5 min and cure at 160 °C for 3 min. No durability tap-water rinsing is assigned to the initial state.

source_location: Official institutional 14-page final published PDF and 22-page supplement. Main p 4 methods and p 6 LOI Table 2; SI p 15 TG Table SI-5, pp 6-8 recipes and p 9 washing. Main method/LOI and SI method/TG pixels reviewed; no graph digitization.
limitations: Eight prepared textile/wash states with sixteen atmospheric TG conditions. All LOI rows are after five simulated home laundry cycles, not unwashed. Table 4 uses representative chemistry names and rounds TPTEPO LOI to 27.4; no add-on or label crosswalk is inferred from that comparison table. Source laundering standard editions conflict; explicit physical wash conditions are retained.

TG_locator: Official supplement p 15, Table SI-5: source Tdonset, explicitly DTG-defined Tdmax and residue at 800 °C for nitrogen and air.
conditions_locator: Final article p 4, sections 2.1 and 2.2.2-2.2.6; SI pp 6-9, sections SI-3.3 through SI-4. TG: approximately 4 mg, 25-800 °C, N2 and air, total gas flow 50 mL/min, 10 °C/min. Wash procedure: SI p 9.
pairing_evidence: Main Table 2 explicitly reports fire tests after five wash cycles. SI-4 states rinsed, dried and conditioned washed samples precede other characterization and analysis. Source describes solution volume as twice fabric weight, without explicit volume units. Steam on a needle frame at 110 °C and 0.4 bar above atmospheric pressure for 1 h. Rinse with warm water for 10 min, dry and condition for 24 h at 20 °C and 65% RH before the accelerated durability wash. Actual P before/after washing is 1.56 ± 0.03% / 1.56 ± 0.04%. One accelerated wash operation simulating five home laundry cycles: sandwich a 152.4 × 50.8 mm specimen between two multifiber test fabrics and stitch the edges. Use 0.225 g ECE 98 detergent, 150 mL demineralized water and 50 steel balls in an Atlas Launder-O-Meter LEF at 49 °C for 45 min. Rinse three times with demineralized water, dry at 60 °C for 2 h and condition in standard atmosphere for 24 h before other characterization. SI-4 prepares three wash specimens per sample. The main and SI heading cite AATCC 61-1996; SI procedural text and silver durability prose cite AATCC 61-2013, so standard edition remains source-conflicted.

source_location: Official institutional 14-page final published PDF and 22-page supplement. Main p 4 methods and p 6 LOI Table 2; SI p 15 TG Table SI-5, pp 6-8 recipes and p 9 washing. Main method/LOI and SI method/TG pixels reviewed; no graph digitization.
limitations: Eight prepared textile/wash states with sixteen atmospheric TG conditions. All LOI rows are after five simulated home laundry cycles, not unwashed. Fifty-wash variants, dry/microwave controls and unused steam recipes lack matched measured TG/LOI and remain held. Table 4 uses representative chemistry names and rounds TPTEPO LOI to 27.4; no add-on or label crosswalk is inferred from that comparison table. Source laundering standard editions conflict; explicit physical wash conditions are retained.

conditions_locator: Final article p 4, sections 2.1 and 2.2.2-2.2.6; SI pp 6-9, sections SI-3.3 through SI-4. TG: approximately 4 mg, 25-800 °C, N2 and air, total gas flow 50 mL/min, 10 °C/min. Wash procedure: SI p 9.

treatment_chemistry: Licorice-root extract with citric acid and disodium hydrogen phosphate, pH 4, applied by padding
treatment_method: Use the article’s plain-woven substrate. Licorice root of the same batch/lot was prewashed with distilled water; the source additionally says 10 g root was mixed with 300 mL distilled water before oven-drying at 75 °C for 24 h and mechanical cutting. Table 1 extraction uses 5 kg licorice root and 20 L of 99% isopropanol, mixed at 900 rpm for 48 h without air contact, then filtered through Macherey-Nagel MN-GF-3 paper. Heat to 85 °C to remove isopropanol. For the padding bath, Table 2 specifies 12 g extract, 0.6 g citric acid monohydrate, 0.6 g disodium hydrogen phosphate and 250 mL pure water, with acetic acid adjusting pH to 4. The Table 2 heading says Quantity (g/kg), despite those individual amounts and volumes; no concentration denominator is silently repaired. Use the Prowhite horizontal padder with 85% wet pickup, dry at 100 °C for 2 min and cure at 150 °C for 2 min. Generic prose mentions acrylate-copolymer binders in the finishing bath, but the padding recipe lists no binder amount; retain that uncertainty instead of borrowing the coating binder recipe.

treatment_chemistry: Table 1 molar ratio DAPPO:ODA:PMDA:BPDA = 0:100:70:30. DAPPO is bis(3-aminophenyl)phenylphosphine oxide; PI1 contains no DAPPO.
treatment_method: Table 1 supplies the individual DAPPO:ODA:PMDA:BPDA molar formulation. PMDA and BPDA were dried before use, ODA used directly and DMAc purified by reduced-pressure distillation. Section 1.2 reports PAA solution formation in DMAc at room temperature for 12 h, 15 wt% solids and inherent viscosity controlled to 1.8–2.5 dL/g. Solution placed in a 2 L spinning pot and left 12 h for degassing, then dry-jet wet spun at room temperature across a 2 cm air gap into a 33 wt% DMAc aqueous coagulation bath, jet stretch ratio 2.5 and subsequent draw ratio 1.5. Figure 1 identifies a 15 wt% DMAc/water washing bath and a second washing bath. PAA fibers thermally imidized at 50–300 °C with gradient heating over 8 h, then drawn 1–3 times at 480 °C to obtain PI fibers. The exact final draw ratio of each table row is not stated. These are the initial prepared fibers; no durability laundering reported.

composition: Source describes plain cotton fabrics, 100%, purchased from Chaotianmen Market in Chongqing, China; yarn and thread specifications not given
sample_state: FRC3, 40 wt% APGDPE bath, 20.8% weight gain, 0 laundering cycles
treatment_chemistry: Ammonium salt 1,3-propylene glycol diphosphate ester (APGDPE), with dicyandiamide catalyst
treatment_method: Synthesize APGDPE from 1,3-propylene glycol (0.100 mol, 7.765 g) and phosphoric acid (0.200 mol, 23.059 g) at 130 °C for 3 h with magnetic stirring; continuously add urea (0.200 mol, 12.012 g), heat at 170 °C for 2.5 h, purify with absolute ethanol, filter and oven-dry at 60 °C; yield approximately 88%. Dissolve APGDPE in distilled water to a 40 wt% bath and add dicyandiamide catalyst, whose amount is not reported. Immerse cotton at 70 °C for 40 min using a 1:20 fabric-mass to bath-volume ratio; pad through a nip to 120% wet pickup, cure at 180 °C for 5 min using an automatic continuous backing machine, rinse with running water and dry at 60 °C for 1 h. No additional precleaning or conditioning protocol is stated.
source_title: One-step Green Synthesis of Eco-friendly Novel N-P Synergistic Flame Retardant for Cotton Fabric
source_location: Complete official 21-page author preprint PDF; pp 3–5 methods and Table 1; pp 6–7 own measured LOI and Table 2; pp 9–11 TG definitions/data and Table 6; Figure 5 p 19 inspected for consistency. Original PDF pixels inspected for methods and Tables 2/6; no graph-estimated values.
limitations: Actual author preprint v1, not journal-verified. Final DOI 10.1007/s10570-021-04049-5 remains related version only with a mandatory future alias/reuse hold; exact final numerical equivalence has not been established. One prepared state is represented by two atmosphere conditions. Dicyandiamide catalyst dosage, initial fabric cleaning, TG aliquot mass/pan/flow and TG/LOI replication and conditioning are not stated. Control LOI is only about 18.0% and is held under the exact-number criterion. FRC1, FRC2 and all post-laundering LOI states lack matching TG. FRC2 after 30 cycles is 30.0 in prose but 30.3 in Table 2, retained as a held conflict. Table 3 contains literature comparators and is not new evidence. Cone calorimetry residues/CVs, FTIR KBr preparation and vertical-test dimensions are not transferred to TG or LOI. limitations: Ten treated source states are extracted under the disclosed original-evidence limits. Only exact own measured LOI and explicit TG are used. No MCC temperatures, heat release rates, vertical-flame char lengths or graph estimates are imported as TG. Table 3 defines onset of degradation, with no fixed mass-loss threshold or maximum-rate equivalence inferred. Own TGA nitrogen/ramp/flow/range come from official SI S2; MCC sample mass and three replicate measurements belong to the separate MCC assay. Table 2 and section 3.2 explicitly distinguish unwashed fabrics 1–7 from washed fabrics 8–18; the general section 2.2 wash description is preserved alongside that specific mapping. The washed group has a 20 min DI-water wash at 40 °C, described also as 10 min × 2, two cold DI-water rinses in section 3.2, and 80 °C drying for 5 min. Repeated treatment counts represent complete treatment, cure, wash and weighing cycles, not extra independent durability washes. Fabric 2 is held for LOI 26 versus prose 27; fabric 10 LOI 27–28 is a range and is held. Fabric 1 has an exact numeric pair but its individual formulation/add-on row was not recovered, so it stays held. Fabric 14 residue is 27.1 in Table 3 versus indexed prose 271; no decimal repair is assumed. The absolute Table 3 onsets for fabrics 10–16 do not agree arithmetically with their listed reductions from the Table 3 control by 0.2 °C; affected canonical onsets stay blank and native values remain raw. Fabric 14 consequently has no retained canonical TG and stays held. Fabric 11 is consistently the two-cycle sodium-carbonate state, but add-on is 14.5 ± 0.3 in Table 2/thermal discussion versus 13.9 in the FTIR discussion and SI Figure S5; no single canonical add-on is assigned. HCl is 2 N in the specific section 3.2 recipe versus generic 5% catalyst wording in section 2.2; both are retained without conversion. Control is held for conservative family QA: related AATCC Review 2012 gives the same LOI 21, same style #423 and TG method, with onset 337.7 and residue 0.36 versus this source 337.2 and 0.4. This near coincidence is not proof of identical measurements, and distinct treated chemistries are not excluded. Source-specific reuse screening found no exact paired-observation match; the related 2009 and 2016 sources remain excluded under their unresolved identifiers. Direct main article retrieval is restricted; original indexed text is cached, while only the official SI has a document hash. Main table and figure pixels have not been verified.

source_location: Complete original nine-page publisher PDF, pp 1–9; methods, Tables 1–4, Figures 1–7, conclusion and all references reviewed. Original pages 2,3,5,6,7,8 inspected as pixels for recipes, conditions, numerical tables, TG profiles and identity.
limitations: Five initial source textile states represented by ten TG conditions, not ten distinct states. Table 4 measured LOI ± values are retained with unspecified uncertainty type; neither SD nor LOI replicate count is inferred. Three repeated measurements and averaging in the source relate to stiffness/air-permeability methods, not expressly to LOI. All R600 values are explicit Tables 2/3 values; the standalone hydrogel residue 34.1% belongs to a nontextile specimen and is excluded. The TC10 nitrogen row prints two T10 values, 228 and 321 °C, across its two stage lines; canonical T10 is blank for that condition, with both raw values retained. T50 and R600 remain independently reported. DTG table temperatures are retained in native fields without assigning canonical decomposition peaks, because first-stage fabric losses are attributed mainly to moisture and unreacted monomers and peak semantics are not independently defined. No stage weight loss is converted into residue. Both Figure 5 axes read Weight loss (%) although the traces descend from about100; the axis wording is preserved and no graph coordinates are used. Canonical TG scan endpoints are blank because methods do not state them; residue assessment is explicitly 600 °C. Air is assigned from the explicit method, Table 2 and Figure 5(a); prose says the untreated fabric is destroyed in an oxygen atmosphere but does not specify a separate pure-O2 assay. This raw wording is retained, not used as another condition or zero-residue claim. Nominal 10/20/30/40% BisMEP labels, introduction mole-ratio wording, source gram amounts and Table 1 mM entries are not mutually resolved; use source-native labels and entries without calculating a corrected loading or retained add-on. For the same 5 mg AAPH, standalone hydrogel synthesis reports 18.4 × 10⁻³ mM but fabric coating reports 1.84 × 10⁻³ mM; both are retained and no exponent or unit is repaired. Drying at 60 °C overnight belongs to standalone hydrogel synthesis, while fabric coating uses70 °C with unspecified duration. TC40L is a distinct after-home-laundry state with LOI 25 ± 0.2 and no corresponding TG; it is held. Source stiffness prose says decreases although its tabulated stiffness rises; this unrelated inconsistency is not used to alter TG or LOI. Source-supplied cotton is not assumed to have an unreported bleach, scour or weave. Numeric reuse search found one common untreated LOI 18/T10 319 in DOI 10.14504/ajr.8.3.5, but its other condition values, preparation and instrument differ; no shared measurement identity is asserted from that partial coincidence. Older private Dahiya2009, washable2016 and 2022 PTAP/PVPA sources have distinct materials/treatment tuples; no source-wide family exclusion or blanket independence claim. Table 3 nitrogen T50 values of 427 °C for TC30 and 358 °C for TC40 conflict with the ordering of Figure 5(b). These two canonical T50 cells are blank; table values remain source-native only. No swapping or graph-derived substitute is used.

source_location: Published main article pp 580–591 accessed through public indexed original text. Own preparation and assay methods, sections 3.4–3.11, Tables 1/2, Figure 12 caption, conclusion and source identity reviewed. No main PDF-byte or pixel claim.
limitations: The extracted pair is the initial untreated silk control only. The published original main text is available through a public indexed mirror; original PDF bytes and figure pixels were not retrieved, so its evidence-cache hash is distinct from an unavailable PDF hash. The source explicitly gives control LOI 24.0% in section 3.4 and control air residue 6.8% at 600 °C in section 3.9. Figure 12 caption identifies separate nitrogen and air experiments. No nitrogen control residue is inferred from a curve. Treated samples are described as mostly losing their weight completely under air; this qualitative group statement is not converted into exact zero residues or assigned to named rows. Table 2 residue values belong to cone calorimetry and are excluded from TG fields. Exact LOIs are also reported for 2 g/L Fe/Ti treatments and 20% owf baicalin/quercetin/rutin treatments, but matching exact TG values are not established. Figure 12 uses 5% owf flavonoids with 2 g/L metal salts; 20% owf flavonoid-only LOIs are not transferred to that prepared state. Treated/mordanted LOIs are otherwise described as above thresholds or about 27%, or shown in figures; none is rounded into an exact state value. Wash durability tests at 10 and 20 cycles remain distinct from initial TG. The reported six tensile replicates, five flexural replicates and 24 h conditioning at 21 ±1 °C and 65 ±5% RH apply to mechanical tests; three replicates and eight fabric layers apply to cone calorimetry. They do not establish LOI/TG replication, conditioning or geometry. The source does not state TG pan, aliquot cutting, LOI dimensions, textile areal density or an earlier scouring procedure for the supplied control. Supplementary figures concern antibacterial/antioxidant behavior and Table S1 concerns mechanical properties; complete SI was not retrieved. A common LOI 24.0 in the earlier silk-silica study does not alone establish shared observations; that accepted source has N2 R600 33.95 with a different gas-flow method, and no exact paired match was found in source-specific screening.

material_form: nonwoven bamboo mat/woven kenaf mat/epoxy laminate
composition: Source 40% total bamboo/kenaf reinforcement at 50:50 in DER-331/JOINTMINE 905-3s epoxy matrix; No added nanoclay
sample_state: B/K/epoxy; initial cured and post-cured textile laminate
treatment_chemistry: No added nanoclay
treatment_method: DGEBA epoxy DER-331 (Dow) and JOINTMINE 905-3s amine hardener were supplied by Tazdiq Engineering, Malaysia. Nanoclay was slowly dispersed in epoxy by mechanical stirring, then high-shear mixed with a T-25 Ultra Turrax homogenizer at 10000 rpm for 30 min in an ice bath and degassed for 30 min. Hardener was added slowly and hand-mixed; resin/hardener ratio is unreported in this original. Nonwoven bamboo mat (Shijiangzhuang Bi Yang Technology, China; source area density 0.8 kg/m²) and woven kenaf mat (ZKK, Malaysia; 0.6 kg/m²) were arranged layer by layer in a 240 × 120 × 3 mm stainless mold. Total fibre loading is source-reported 40%, with bamboo:kenaf 50:50; exact ply count/order is unreported. The mats were impregnated with the resin mixture and hand-rolled to remove bubbles, cured at room temperature for 24 h, then post-cured at 105 °C for 5 h. The unfilled control was made by the same method.
source_title: Thermo-oxidative stability and flammability properties of bamboo/kenaf/nanoclay/epoxy hybrid nanocomposites
source_location: Complete original RSC publisher HTML: title through conclusions and 65 references, Tables 1–10 and figure captions. No full PDF-byte or figure-pixel claim.
limitations: Four finished textile-laminate formulations are represented by the same source labels in the preparation, experimental TG Tables 5/6 and measured LOI Table 8. The source separately studies nanoclay powders and epoxy/nanoclay morphology; those component data are not substituted for the laminate TG. Oxygen atmosphere is retained as reported, without relabeling it as air. The source LOI is measured by an ASTM oxygen-concentration series; CF+k d is its standard series calculation. The later regression between char and measured LOI does not make these char-calculated LOIs. Table 8 explicitly reports standard deviations, but does not explain their averaging basis; the 15-specimen group and final 5-specimen sequence are preserved without inventing independent repetitions. Table 8 CF/d column units are incorrectly printed as°C while the methods define vol% oxygen. Whole-number LOIs 20/23/28 in narrative summaries are rounded descriptions; the precise Table 8 values are retained. Nanoclay fraction denominator, resin/hardener ratio, exact ply count/order, TG aliquot mass/pan/preparation and LOI conditioning are unreported. The preparation shares a broader bamboo/kenaf/epoxy family with earlier thermal/mechanical/weathering studies; their methods or numerical values are not transferred, and any future control reuse requires observation-specific review. The complete publisher HTML is available; PDF bytes and original figure pixels are unavailable. Thermal table values are transcribed, without estimating graph coordinates. The thermal prose difference of 60 °C between 495 and 434 is arithmetically imprecise; neither table temperature is altered. The cone TTI narrative/table mismatch is retained outside the TG–LOI extraction.

limitations: Two initial manufactured structures are represented at the first, room-temperature LOI point. The publisher provides public Figure 2 and Figure 9 images with explicit numerical labels; these labels are transcribed directly, without extracting coordinates or calculating residue. The original main text is available as an indexed published author copy; main PDF bytes are unavailable. Figure 2 prints integer DTG peak temperatures, while the accompanying prose describes them as close to those temperatures; both source presentations are preserved. The source explicitly assays the finished laminate and foam-core sandwich composite. The exact textile weave and TG aliquot cutting, grinding, mass and through-thickness sampling are unreported. The source describes PAN-CF T300-3000 wet-layup plies, not a short-fiber-filled resin specimen. Cure, cooling, fiber fraction and conditioning are unreported. No numeric ambient temperature is inferred from the first LOI point position. The additional elevated-temperature LOI points are retained separately and are not additional preparation states. The three cone repetitions and five vertical/three horizontal burn repetitions are not assigned to TG or LOI. Stage intervals and stage mass losses are not T5 or an extrapolated onset. Table 3 and Figure 6 mass-retention values are from cone calorimetry, not TG; all canonical residues remain blank. Figure 2 rates have units percent per °C, which are not percent per minute. No wash, thermal aging or post-fire specimen is assigned to the initial pair. Related later carbon/epoxy sandwich work uses separate specimens and methods and requires its own observation-level review.

sample_state: S1; initial four-ply laminate; 0 wt% MH and 0 wt% CH
treatment_chemistry: Polyester resin with magnesium hydroxide (MH) or calcium hydroxide (CH) nanoparticles as assigned in Table 1; no additional textile finishing step
treatment_method: Bi-directional woven flax fabric and MH/CH nanoparticles of nominal average size 30 nm were acquired from Go Green Enterprises, Chennai, India. Polyester resin, hardener and accelerator were supplied by Kovai Cheenu Enterprises, Coimbatore, India. The nanoparticles were dispersed in styrene monomer by ultrasonication for 30 min followed by magnetic stirring for 30 min, then mixed with polyester resin and source-reported 2 wt.% cobalt accelerator plus 2 wt.% MEKP. Styrene quantity and the two curing-agent percentage denominators are unreported; Table 1 nominal polyester/flax/filler fractions already sum to 100% and are not renormalized. Four 300 × 300 mm woven flax plies were manually impregnated, stacked in a release-wax-coated mild-steel mold and held at 2 MPa at room temperature for 72 h. Panels were post-cured at 50 °C for 2 h. No durability wash or post-fire preparation is assigned.

source_location: Indexed original SciELO journal HTML and published author-uploaded main text: sections 2.1–2.7, 3.4–3.5, Table 1, Table 3, Table 5 and conclusions. Original Figure 7/8 pixels and complete PDF bytes unavailable.
limitations: The original tables and state-specific prose support three initial prepared textile-laminate pairs. Evidence is from indexed original journal HTML and the published author-uploaded text; complete PDF bytes and Figure 7/8 pixels are unavailable. No numerical values are derived from plotted coordinates. The source gives an own measured LOI method and mean of three trials, without dispersion. The separate mechanical-test count of five is not assigned to TG or LOI. TG aliquot preparation, pan and replicate count are unreported. Onset is the source-defined To without a specified mass-loss threshold or tangent algorithm. Table 1 nominal composition is preserved; styrene and curing-agent mass bases are not reconstructed. The source makes inaccurate broad group claims: S4 and S6 are called hybrid MH–CH specimens in the conclusion, although Table 1 and the exact LOI paragraph assign them solely to MH and CH, respectively. The same conclusion gives a >24.4% LOI threshold for S10, whereas the exact results paragraph gives 24.4%; S10 is excluded. Higher-level claims that all residues increase or that S4/S7/S10 are the respective largest residues are not fully consistent with the individual Table 3 entries. No cross-sample values are corrected from those claims. Several cone, burn-time, burning-rate and mechanical summary statements disagree with their tables or units; none of those measurements is used as TG or LOI. The other six treated samples lack exact recoverable numerical LOIs outside unavailable Figure 8 and remain excluded.
